title: Bayesian A/B Experimentation Engine
problem: Fixed-horizon frequentist experiment evaluation forces product teams to wait for arbitrary precalculated sample thresholds before taking business actions, prolonging exposure to inferior variants and encouraging ad-hoc peeking that inflates false discovery rates. Continuous inspection under frequentist methods invalidates standard p-values unless complex alpha-spending functions are maintained. A Bayesian sequential experimentation engine continuously models parameter posteriors, computing the exact probability of variant superiority and quantifying bounded expected loss to automate candidate variant promotion or termination while strictly controlling decision risk.
use_cases: Continuous feature-flag variant evaluation for web and mobile customer checkout workflows
Pricing tier optimization with automated risk-bounded stopping thresholds
Recommendation model candidate comparison without fixed sample horizon delays
hard_parts: Preventing discovery bias during small-sample cold starts where high variance can trigger premature stopping without minimum sample guards
Computing two-dimensional numerical quadrature for expected loss integrals within sub-20ms HTTP API response constraints
Handling concurrent atomic increment transactions on experiment arms under SQLite without database lock contention
Calibrating sequential stopping boundaries via Monte Carlo simulations to maintain Type I error rates under null conditions
screener_signals: Deterministic pytest test suite comparing closed-form posterior probabilities against SciPy numerical quadrature
Automated Monte Carlo simulation script reproducing bounded false positive rates across 500 null experiment runs
Standalone reproducible FastAPI service with SQLite transactional persistence and benchmark reports

architecture.data_flow: Client telemetry emits exposure and conversion events to FastAPI; API writes atomic increment transactions to SQLite; Decision Gateway triggers Posterior Evaluation Engine; SciPy computes Beta conjugate updates and Expected Loss; engine returns continue, promote, or terminate status based on calibrated decision thresholds.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Automated status transitions to STOPPED_WINNER or STOPPED_INCONCLUSIVE when sample size exceeds minimum threshold and expected loss drops below target epsilon.

targets.method: Vectorized 2D numerical quadrature comparison against closed-form incomplete beta function
targets.input: 15 deterministic synthetic test parameter pairs covering extreme and balanced beta distributions
targets.minimum_pass: Absolute error < 1e-4 across 15 of 15 test parameter pairs
targets.target: Absolute error < 1e-5 across 15 of 15 test parameter pairs
targets.report: Pytest numerical tolerance test log file with residual errors

targets.metric: Empirical Type I Error under Null Distribution
targets.method: Monte Carlo sequential experiment simulation over identical arms with conversion rate 0.05
targets.input: 500 simulated experiment trajectories with minimum sample threshold of 200 observations per arm
targets.minimum_pass: Empirical false stopping rate <= 5.0% across 500 simulated null trials
targets.target: Empirical false stopping rate <= 4.2% across 500 simulated null trials
targets.report: CSV simulation summary table and empirical cumulative distribution plot

targets.method: Locust load benchmark simulating concurrent decision requests against running FastAPI service
targets.input: 1,000 synthetic HTTP GET requests across 50 concurrent active experiment states
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, SQLite WAL mode, local loopback
targets.minimum_pass: p95 latency < 35ms under 100 requests per second
targets.target: p95 latency < 18ms under 100 requests per second
targets.report: Locust HTML execution summary report and CSV percentile export

starter_input.spec: Deterministic synthetic traffic generator creating exposure events and binary conversion events with configurable ground-truth arm probabilities.
starter_input.size: 10,000 synthetic event records across 4 test experiments with seeded conversion rates
starter_input.seeded_cases: Extreme low-conversion rate (0.001 vs 0.002), high-traffic parity null (0.05 vs 0.05), and early high-variance noise bursts
starter_input.label_source: Deterministic pseudorandom generator with fixed random seed 42
starter_input.personal_data_policy: Strictly synthetic user identifiers (random UUIDs); no personal or real user tracking data used

worksheet.q1: The student builds a self-contained Bayesian sequential A/B experimentation service that processes event streams, continuously computes Beta-Binomial conjugate posteriors and expected loss quadrature, and automates early stopping decisions.
worksheet.q2: Core path: analytical Beta-Binomial posterior, expected loss quadrature, SQLite state persistence, FastAPI endpoints, Monte Carlo null simulator, and anti-fake verification. Extended path: hierarchical shrinkage priors and continuous Gaussian reward metrics (+12h).
worksheet.q3: Components: Posterior Math (5h), Stopping Logic (5h), FastAPI API (4h), Monte Carlo Harness (4h), Benchmark Harness (4h), Docs & Buffer (3h). Subtotal 25h x 1.15 = 29h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: ML training, API/backend. Metrics built: Expected Loss Quadrature Accuracy, Empirical Type I Error under Null, Decision Endpoint Latency. Rejected: live streaming cluster lag (no Kafka/Flink required for core Bayesian engine).
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: quadrature latency under concurrency, discovery bias on small sample cold starts, SQLite locking under concurrent writes, calibrating epsilon stopping thresholds.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: synthetic exposure and binary conversion generator with fixed RNG seed (NumPy PCG64, seed 42), 10,000 synthetic records, extreme skew edge cases, no personal data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware & Environment: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, no external cloud accounts or quotas. Fallback: local venv with in-memory SQLite.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: 2D numerical quadrature latency in expected loss. Fallback: 1D vectorized quadrature approximation with precomputed lookup grids.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: hardcoded JSON responses for posterior or false positive rates. Rubric item 5 (anti-fake) accepts a dynamic random seed from screener and recomputes all mathematical distributions on the fly.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Not required for purely synthetic simulated A/B testing data; synthetic user IDs only.
